Subject: Service boundary checklist & next-step POC (Dedicated vs Private VPC)

Hi Claire — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap plus a short checklist so we can align on the right deployment mode (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC) and next steps for a pilot.

Call recap (high level)
- MedSys Health has PHI workloads (billing + clinical notes).
- Primary objective: strict tenant isolation + US-only data residency.
- Secondary: customer-managed KMS (BYOK) preferred and SSO via AAD.
- Timeline: pilot goal = 6–8 weeks; production decision in Q1.

Key clarification asks (helps us map to Dedicated vs Private VPC)
1) Data residency: confirm all data must stay within US regions (yes/no).
2) Network: do you require a private control plane (control plane in your VPC) or is VPC peering + strict egress rules acceptable?
3) KMS: is BYOK mandatory for model keys and logs? If BYOK is optional, what level of assurance do you need (HSM-backed, key rotation policy)?
4) Audit & retention: required audit log retention period and whether logs must be accessible from your SIEM.
5) Pen testing & compliance: do you require vendor-performed annual pentest and/or onboarding evidence beyond SOC2 (e.g., FedRAMP or HITRUST controls)?

Based on answers we usually recommend one of two practical paths:
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) with VPC peering, private subnets, and BYOK for storage/encryption: faster to stand up, full isolation at the inference layer, control plane remains in Redwood (we can offer strict egress controls and separate tenancy).
- Private (customer-managed control plane / on-prem): complete control over control plane and networking, preferred for highest regulatory isolation but adds setup + ops time.

Recommended immediate next steps
- Please fill/return the security questionnaire you shared on the call (I attached a blank copy to the call notes; if you prefer, send your completed one).
- Marcus (cc) to propose a short tech mapping doc and an initial POC Bill of Materials.
- Quick follow-up engineering call next week — suggest Thu 10/23 11:00am ET or Fri 10/24 9:00am ET. Which works for you?

I attached a short one-pager checklist we use to map customers to Dedicated vs Private (will send Marcus' technical notes and BOM after he reviews).

Vanessa — thanks for the clear recap. Confirmations below and I attached our completed security questionnaire.

- Data residency: must be US-only. All PHI data must not leave US regions.
- Network: preferred option is Private control plane, but we will accept Dedicated with strict network egress controls and documented isolation if the control plane remains vendor-managed.
- KMS: BYOK is preferred and in some cases mandatory for long-term production. For pilot we can evaluate vendor-managed keys if we get a BYOK commitment for prod. HSM-backed keys required for production.
- Audit & retention: logs retained for 7 years; SIEM access via secure export (S3 with our cross-account role) required.
- Pen testing & compliance: SOC2 Type II required plus a brief vendor security questionnaire. HITRUST not required today but may be on roadmap.

We want to prioritize speed to pilot but not at the expense of getting commitments on BYOK and US-only residency for production. Attached: MedSys_Security_Questionnaire_Filled.pdf

Available for Thu 10/23 11:00am ET for the engineering call.

Hi Claire — appreciate the fast turn-around and the completed questionnaire (received). Quick technical mapping to help the call tomorrow:

Short summary (technical)
- Dedicated capacity + VPC peering
  - What we can deliver quickly: dedicated GPU nodes in a separate tenancy with VPC peering, private subnets, and no public egress routes from inference hosts.
  - BYOK: supported for storage and logging via customer KMS (we integrate with major KMS providers; HSM-backed keys supported).
  - Control plane: remains in Redwood; we will provide an SLA and written egress/fallback policy.
  - Pros: fastest to pilot (2–3 week setup), lower initial ops overhead.
  - Cons: control plane remains vendor-managed (some customers accept this with contract commitments).

- Private (customer-managed control plane / VPC-hosted)
  - What we can deliver: control plane components deployed into your VPC (private control plane), optional on-prem package for air-gapped sites.
  - BYOK & network: full BYOK and local key management, no egress to Redwood control plane if required.
  - Pros: highest isolation and regulatory fit.
  - Cons: longer setup (4–8+ weeks), requires network & ops engagement on your side.

Practical recommendation for MedSys Health
- Run a two-step approach: pilot on Dedicated with contractual BYOK commitment for production and US-only residency guarantees. While pilot runs, we prepare a Private control plane plan for production if you want end-to-end isolation. This balances speed vs. risk.

POC checklist (items we need from MedSys to run Dedicated POC)
- Completed security questionnaire (received).
- Target dataset sample (anonymized) and expected token volumes (for throughput sizing).
- VPC CIDR ranges and preferred peering/endpoint model.
- KMS contact + key provisioning preferences (BYOK flow).
- SIEM integration details (S3 cross-account role ARN or preferred export).

Estimated timelines
- Dedicated POC: 2–3 weeks from signed POC Statement of Work and access items above.
- Private control plane assessment: concurrent architecture review, 3–6 weeks to finalize BOM and timeline; hands-on deployment 4–8+ weeks depending on approvals.

I attached a short BOM for the Dedicated POC (Redwood_POC_BOM.xlsx) and a draft scope we can use for the SOW. Happy to walk through line-by-line on the call.
